payload.acceptance_criteria: a repository whose config already names the managed core gets no advice line for that file, and a repository that does not still gets it - the second half asserted, or the fix is a suppression rather than a check
payload.description:
When install finishes in a repository that already excludes the managed core from its linters, I want it to say nothing, so I can stop training a consumer to skim the region where a tracked CI edit is also reported.

Found by the terminal canary, filed there as term-ip2wz and pressed after it shipped twice unchanged. scaffolds.install_notes tests only whether a config file exists, never what it contains, so it advises extend-exclude on a .ruff.toml that has carried exactly that for releases. The canary verified the exclusion is genuinely in force rather than merely present: ruff format --check over the managed core exits 0 on 54 files.

The same block tells a consumer to hand-edit .pre-commit-config.yaml in a run that separately reports it has just rewritten that file.

Severity is low and nothing fails. The reason it is worth fixing is where it sits: the advice is the tail of the install output, and the tail is also where a re-pin of a tracked CI workflow is announced. Unactionable boilerplate beside a real edit teaches a reader to skip both.

Recorded against myself: this was already a requirement on basicly-fmgwtwi, which is still open, and I shipped two releases without meeting it while telling the canary it was on the record. It was on the record and it was not done.
payload.requirements: the check reads the file rather than testing its presence. A false skip is possible if the path is named for some other reason, and that is accepted and stated rather than guarded, because the cost of a missed note is one line a consumer can still read in the documentation.
payload.title: read the file before advising a change it already carries

payload.acceptance_criteria: external-facts says the control is built from a failure that has been seen rather than an assumed one, and says to check the denominator moved; the always-on surfaces stay under their caps and the projection gates pass
payload.description:
When an agent runs a positive control and it returns zero, I want the rule to say what the control must be built from, so I can stop reading a control's own zero as confirmation.

Asked for by the terminal canary as term-2vkce, and the request is well founded: the rule is in managed core they may never edit, they followed both halves of it, and still got a false reading. The wording said run a positive control and that if the control is empty too the zero belongs to the probe. It never said what the control must be built from.

Their case is the evidence. They planted a table they called ragged; it was valid compact style, so it was never a violation, reported zero, and read exactly like a dead probe. Rebuilt from the defect actually observed - padded cells over an unpadded delimiter row - it reported two errors. What rescued the diagnosis was the denominator: 151 files became 152 when the control was added, which proved the file was read and sent them to the table rather than the tooling.

Three of my own false zeros the same day were the environment answering instead of the code. Theirs is the subtler one and the one the rule did not cover.

Carrying it in their overlay was the fallback, and the objection to that is right: two copies of one rule drift, and ours is the copy every other consumer reads.
payload.requirements: the amendment sits in the existing bullet rather than adding one, because the always-on budget is a standing cost on every consumer. The token cost declared on the fragment is updated to what the projection measures rather than left to drift.
payload.title: amend the positive control rule with what a control must be built from
